content.overview: BNS s. 18 — Accident in doing a lawful act.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Accident in doing a lawful act. BNS restatement of IPC 80. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 80. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 18 is the rule on “Accident in doing a lawful act”. The section provides that nothing is an offence which is done by accident or misfortune, and without any criminal intention or knowledge in the doing of a lawful act in a lawful manner by lawful means and with proper care and caution. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 18 exists so that “Accident in doing a lawful act” has a closed legal test in Chapter III — General Exceptions. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: When an act is not an offence: mistake, accident, infancy, unsoundness, consent, compulsion — and the right of private defence.

The provision in detail
18. Nothing is an offence which is done by accident or misfortune, and without any criminal intention or knowledge in the doing of a lawful act in a lawful manner by lawful means and with proper care and caution

Essential ingredients
1. Nothing is an offence which is done by accident or misfortune, and without any criminal intention or knowledge in the doing of a lawful act in a lawful manner by lawful means and with proper care and caution

Statutory illustrations
Illustration (a). A is at work with a hatchet; the head flies off and kills a man who is standing by. Here, if there was no want of proper caution on the part of A, his act is excusable and not an offence

Exam use: quote illustration (a), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 18 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 18 (Accident in doing a lawful act), Chapter III — General Exceptions.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Nothing is an offence which is done by accident or misfortune, and without any criminal intention or knowledge in the doing of a lawful act in a lawful manner by lawful means and with proper care and caution
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 18 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 18 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

learningObjectives: State the accident exception in BNS s.18.
Apply every condition: accident or misfortune, no criminal intention or knowledge, lawful act, lawful manner, lawful means, and proper care and caution.
Use the hatchet illustration without treating it as a reported case.
enhancement.definition: BNS s.18 provides that nothing is an offence which is done by accident or misfortune, and without any criminal intention or knowledge, in the doing of a lawful act in a lawful manner by lawful means and with proper care and caution.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Accident is an exception only when the whole statutory chain is present. A harmful result is not enough. The act itself must be lawful, done lawfully, by lawful means, with proper care, and without criminal intention or knowledge.
statutoryFramework: Chapter III — General Exceptions, BNS s.18.
The harm is by accident or misfortune.
There is no criminal intention or knowledge in doing the act.
The act is lawful, done in a lawful manner, by lawful means.
Proper care and caution are used.
Illustration: A is at work with a hatchet; the head flies off and kills a man standing by. If there was no want of proper caution, the act is excusable and not an offence.
essentialIngredients: The result occurs by accident or misfortune.
The doer has no criminal intention or knowledge in the doing of the act.
It is done in a lawful manner and by lawful means.
Proper care and caution are present. Want of caution defeats the exception.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 18 is narrow. The section does not say that every unintended death or injury is excusable. The result must be by accident or misfortune, and the doing of the act must be without criminal intention or knowledge. The act, the manner and the means must all be lawful, and there must be proper care and caution. The hatchet illustration is the model: A is doing lawful work, the head flies off, and a bystander is killed. The illustration itself makes the result depend on there being no want of proper caution. If the hatchet was known to be loose and A continued, the caution condition fails. If the act was itself unlawful, s.18 is not the exception to argue. Students should list the conditions separately rather than stopping at the word accident.
examples: Statutory illustration, labelled as illustration: A is at work with a hatchet; the head flies off and kills a bystander. If there was no want of proper caution, the act is excusable.
Teaching contrast: A knows the head is loose and still swings the hatchet beside a crowd. The proper-care condition is in issue and may fail.
Teaching contrast: A is committing an unlawful assault when the weapon slips and injures a third person. The lawful-act condition is missing, so s.18 should not be assumed.
distinctions: Accident under s.18 is not the same as an act likely to cause harm done to avoid greater harm under s.19.
Absence of intention is not enough. Lawful act, lawful manner, lawful means and proper caution are also required.
The hatchet illustration is statutory, not a case name.
problemApplication: Issue: whether the harm is no offence under s.18.
Rule: accident or misfortune; no criminal intention or knowledge; lawful act, manner and means; proper care and caution.
Application: test each condition. Failure of caution or lawfulness ends the exception.
Conclusion: state which condition succeeds or fails. Do not treat 'accident' as a one-word defence.

shortAnswer: List lawful act, manner, means and proper caution.
sixteenMark: Introduction and why accident is not a general excuse.
Proper care, with the illustration and a caution-failure contrast.

keyTakeaways: Every condition in s.18 must be present.
Want of proper caution defeats the exception.
An unlawful act is outside the illustration's reasoning.
